[b]6th January 2167 - Erene - Federation Central Communications Headquarters[/b]

[i]"S-Sir, there is something seriously wrong with our systems to Korrin."[/i] A young and pale operator softly spoke up, sitting at one desk of the open central command room, surrounded by hundreds of screens and open communication channels with the planets and moons of the Federation.

Approaching him was a senior Federation officer, who pressed down on the operator's table and leaned forward to the readings shown on his computer. [i]"When did this happen?"[/i] The officer asked and turned to the operator.

[i]"Just now, sir. They just suddenly stopped with no warning or anything. I'm trying to reopen communications, but the Korrin systems are refusing."[/i]

The officer stood back and placed his right hand on his chin, slightly stroking his beard as he pondered for a moment, his gaze moving to the front screens and the offices of the command room. [i]"Must be Kartovsky particles messing up their systems. Wait a day and report back to me, if nothing changes, then we'll investigate further."[/i] The officer said in an uninterested and monotone voice, his eyes tired from the busy days at work.

The operator nodded and turned back to his screen, a slight unease in his mind. [i]"Must be the particles, nothing else."[/i]

[b]7th January 2167 - Aktus Sphere - Korrin - Korr City[/b]

Nearly 24 hours had passed since all communications between Erene and Korrin were abruptly ended. To the Federation, it at most just seemed like a severe instance of Kartovsky disruptions, though they were beginning to worry that the colony was going through a major shutdown due to the electromagnetic disruptions. In the months leading up to the communication disruption, the Local Korrin Authority, led by Zytan Hoffmann, had increasingly made negative remarks against the Federation, and relations between Erene and the colony were beginning to sour. While alarming to some members of the Federation, they were under the impression that no significant independence movement was brewing on the moon, and most ignored Korrin's slow efforts to distance itself from Erene. These disruptions in communications between Erene and its colonies beyond the belt were observed in Pallaeon, Aceldama, and even as far as Zeon, though nothing more was thought of other than an increase in Kartovsky activity.

Yet this shutdown of communication was just the start of Zytan's 11 years of scheming. Once Erene was left in the dark, he ordered for his long-awaited independence to begin. The Local Korrin Authority was unanimously dissolved by its members and reformed into the Assembly of the Republic of Korrin. Its first action was to authorise the mobilisation of the military to seize control of the moon and arrest any elements in the administration and military that were still loyal to the Federation. Warships blockaded Korrin while mobile suits were scrambled to patrol for anyone escaping. Institutions around Korrin were seized, and the military announced the independence of the moon, which was met with overwhelming support from the Spacenoid population. By the end of the 24 hours, any remnants of the Federation were wiped clean from the moon, and Zytan prepared to face the Federation...

Vissarius hurriedly ran through the hallways of the Korrin Government Palace, weaving himself past soldiers as he rushed out of the building and onto the balcony that faced the Pioneer Memorial and parade grounds. His black-tinted sunglasses shielded his eyes from the bright lights of the underground facility, which illuminated the parade square and the government plaza, and standing in front of him were a dozen high-ranking officers of the army and navy, who themselves were positioned behind Zytan, who was looking down at the grounds from the balcony. Amongst the officers was his father, Virren Kaifferon, Commander of the Eastern Sector and a close ally to Zytan.

Vissarius adjusted his collar and calmly approached his father, positioning himself to his left side as he cleared his throat and placed both his hands on the metal rails of the balcony. [i]"I hope I haven't missed the parade."[/i]

Virren would notice his son's presence and turn his head towards him. [i]"The parade is after Zytan's speech."[/i] He took a moment to eye Vissarius up and down, then he sighed. [i]"Where the hell were you? We're just about to start, and only now do you show up."[/i]

Vissarius shook his head. [i]"Had to deal with something real quick. A few of the Fed loyalists tried escaping to deep space."[/i]

Virren raised his left eyebrow, intensifying his gaze. [i]"And...? What happened to them?"[/i]

[i]"Well, I got in my mobile suit and flew straight and fast as I could...and destroyed them."[/i] He replied with a slight snicker.

Virren sighed deeply and turned back to the parade grounds. [i]"The objective was to capture them all; they are still bargaining chips. The Federation may be more willing to trade these people for peace, and blowing them all up lowers our chance for a bloodless independence. But no matter, if no other options were available, then we can excuse their deaths."[/i]

Vissarius scoffed and turned his attention down to the parade square, where a large crowd in the tens of thousands stood packed tightly together, as they chanted towards the revolutionaries of Korrin. The crowd stretched throughout every street in the underground sections of Korr City, made up of soldiers, mechanics, women, and even children, all waiting with bated breath for the words of Zytan. Mobile suits stood motionless in the distance within their hangars; Vissarius could spot the faint silhouettes of their crew standing on walkways watching the palace closely. All eyes and ears of Korrin looked to the balcony upon which the independence would be proclaimed.

Zytan finally stepped forward to a large golden microphone, and his presence caused the crowd to erupt into thunderous applause, with Vissarius and the rest of the Korrino officials joining in the applause. For a few seconds the ground shook from the clapping of the people, and it would take half a minute for the place to quiet down as Zytan took a moment to prepare. He adjusted his collar and cleared his throat.

[i]"My father was a young man when he was forced off-world and thrust into becoming a colonial beyond the Belt. At 20 he became a pioneer, landing on this moon and in this very city; back then this was nothing but a resource outpost. He was a young pioneer who longed for home, but as this place grew and Korr City was finally built, he came to love this home more than Erene. My father was a hard-working pioneer, through decades of service, he helped build this home for us all.

All of us have rich stories of our pioneer ancestors, those who left Erene, sometimes forcefully, into uncharted land for what would be the rest of their lives. Our history has been filled with brave pioneers, brave men and women who strived towards a better tomorrow for themselves and their descendants. Their blood courses through our veins, and they look upon us with smiles on their faces as they watch us continue their march, their hopes.

We are new people! The Spacenoids! Our distinct identity has been suppressed by the Erene Federation, who have attempted to trample on Korrino identity and who view us like nothing more than a way for them to hog the resources of Ardagan! Our Spacenoid brothers and sisters on other moons have faced similar conditions, and the Federation continues to live in bliss, ignoring the rise of new people and cultures.

The Federation doesn't care about us! Doesn't care about Korrin or its people! All it cares about are resources and the natural wealth of our home. They will suck us dry, and then once we have nothing to send back to Erene, they will discard us and let us rot! They will turn our world like theirs, a depleted and sad planet on the brink of collapse. While we are hard at work to provide them with everything, the Erenite upper class, the elites, live in luxury and opulence. Our resources fund their rich lives while they give us few things in return. This exploitation cannot go on. And no longer shall we live like this!"[/i] Zytan raised his clenched right hand into a fist and thrust it into the air, the crowd cheering loudly and mimicking his movement.

[i]"The Erene Federation is a bloated and corrupt body, one that slowly rots and lives off the exploitation of the working Spacenoid man! It has been nearly 90 years since the corrupt elites of Erene, consumed by greed, forced many people into slaving away for their easy lives"[/i] Zytan paused for a moment, taking a deep breath, lowering his fist towards his heart.

[i]"We want our freedom! Never forget the times the Federation has trampled us and abused us! Never forget the sacrifices of our people! We, the people of Korrin, the Jovian Republic of Korrin, want independence! Our struggle against the Federation for independence will be hard, but we are ready to fight!

We must send them a message. Not with a message of words but a message of force! There is no point in words anymore, the ears of the Federation elite have been blocked by fat! If they do not accept our independence, if they do not accept the independence of all Spacenoids beyond the belt, then we must deliver them a decisive battle! If the Federation ignores the will of the Spacenoids, we will deliver them death and defeat!"[/i] Zytan raised both his arms into the air, as if embracing the skies themselves. Vissarius and Virren both placed their fists on their chests and shouted alongside the Chancellor.

[i]"Never forget! The greatest tribute we can give to the pioneers and those who have sacrificed themselves is to fight and bring victory to Korrin! Our cause for independence is a valiant one, and it shall bring us victory! Rise! Rise! Rise for independence! Rise for Korrin!" [/i]The crowd all shouted in unison, their fists raised to the skies, their hatred and contempt turned into strength to chant the words...

[b][i]"SIEG KORRIN!"

"SIEG KORRIN!"

"SIEG KORRIN!"[/i][/b]
[/spoiler]

[pre]The Federation had forgotten what it means to struggle. Has anyone ever told you that loneliness sometimes comes from being at the top? That's what the Federation was. A lonely giant. However, what they don't tell you is that this loneliness is a walled garden. Stay alone in the peaceful place of your last victory and time seems to stop, and you'll be none the wiser. One of these days, you'll randomly wake up in a cold sweat and notice that the garden had gone and that the summit of your life's glory had been eclipsed a long, long time ago.[/pre]

[spoiler=[b]Starbound RP | A cancerous growth[/b]][b]STARBOUND RP

A cancerous growth

7 January 2167[/b]

The League of the Orange Creek was named after its most populous O'Neill Cylinder (ONC), ONC Orange Creek. Like a metonym that just never went away. The official name of our "country" is the League of Official Corporate Units and Settlements, though no one really bothers using it. Not even the pretty acronym, LOCUS. Apart from the Orange Creek itself, there's also ONCs Bastione founded by the Sanguinians, Tulevik by the Gythenans, and then finally Huzanak and Sameyasip, the two newer ones created by the Vespurians during the Migration period.

If you had to ask the residents of all five cylinders how they'd rate life in the cylinders, you'd usually get the same middling answers. "Could be worse", "It's alright", "Whatever", "Get that mic off my face." In general, most people wake up without much sense of purpose, typically waking up with their entire day, no, maybe entire week planned out ahead of them. It was the worst form of omniscience that drained all meaning from life.

As if the League understood the purpose of meaning.

Let's say that meaning is in the pursuit of happiness. 

What exactly does this pursuit entail? Is it a horizontal process, a sort of distributive justice to exact comfort over a great multitude? But that's life in the Orange Creek. In this small, cylindrical refrigerator in outer space, every man and woman lives their entire lives without ever stepping foot on natural ground. A circular economy is a cruel but necessary thing. Every bath is metered, every meal rationed, and every moment of bliss offset to ensure that waste flows back into the closed system. 

We don't even keep graveyards to preserve memories of the past, bodies get cremated. Ever since the O'Neill Cylinders finished construction, it's like Oranics had been left frozen in time.

So then, I guess the pursuit of happiness is vertical then? A despairing pit that we climb out of towards a waiting salvation? But this was the pursuit of the old ways. A kind of horrible utilitarianism that builds a utopia by processing the carcasses of the sacrificed into the perfect foundation. Funnily enough, the Orange Creek suffers from this too. Not in the cylinder itself, where the corpos get to live their lives without worry, but outside, where contractual workers and clones alike toil and labor to keep the mundane paradise alive, but quietly.

Point is, the League of the Orange Creek isn't all that great. And yet, on every sign and on every board, you keep saying the same mottos. Omnia omibus, "All things to all men", as if proclaiming to the world that in this cylinder is humanity in its idealized form, cloistered, closed, but self-sufficiency, which meets the needs of the people without sacrificing the capacity of future generations to do the same.

The corpos on high though, they knew the real purposes of the Orange Creek. Euphrasia herself knew it very, very well. The League owes its existence solely to the cancerous growth.

- - -

Euphrasia stepped out of 11 League Park with a beleaguered expression. This was her default expression after most boardroom meetings to be fair, but this summary agenda had been particularly grueling. She began things on the morning of the 6th of January, and now it was the 7th. An entire day, completely spent within the confines of a corporate building, listening to case after case, all of them presented either by SummitONE or a certain Gale FitzDavid. 

How would you feel if the worst person you've ever known received a standing ovation? What about three times, in front of some of the most important figures you'll ever know? Tough, how about an entire day! This is how boardroom meetings in the League have always gone.

[list]

"Cheer up, Euphy." Euphemia chuckled, walking beside her sister as they stepped down from the front entrance. "Look, I know you hate Mr. FitzDavid, but SummitONE's wins are the wins of the League! And besides, he was being 100% legit too, I could tell. Mobile suits are the future of warfare, they're literally too cool not to be."

"I'm not disputing his case on the mobile suits, Mia." Euphrasia replied, clearly annoyed by Euphemia's prattling.

"Then what's with that face? You'd make a preschool cry if they seeya like that!"

"It's a face that says we're due for another cancerous growth."

"Cance-... wha?"

"Look, it's your friends." says Euphrasia, pointing to a small group of executives waiting at the maglev platform.

"Oh shoot!"

[/list]

Without missing a beat, Euphemia suddenly ran off with such speed that seemed almost physically impossible given the equally formal getup she was in. But alas, Euphrasia had learned to stop wondering how her sister does anything at all.

Euphrasia stopped before walking up to the maglev platform, still wary of where she was to go next and instead peered over the high railings of the walkway and looked up into the curving horizon of the Orange Creek and wondered if it was worth to sleepwalk blindly into duller days if it meant she could ignore what SummitONE kept doing. What Gale kept doing. There was a wicked sense of comfort in just resting your head and shutting off in the face of great injustice.

That said, it wasn't very easy to shut off when the greatest enemy that must be destroyed was a pale-faced show-off who dressed in the exact opposite way of yourself.

Gale stepped out of 11 League Park last with his network of SummitONE executives, the bulk of them just old friends of his from his younger days. Most wouldn't be able to tell at a glance though given what they looked like. Tall, pale-faced, some with white hair, and with those slightly larger eyes that burned into your soul. Generational Spacenoids. Nowadays they're ubiquitous in the Ardagan System, though on the ONCs they're still a sort of oddity, typically restricted to those families that have been here since the very beginning, or else those that just didn't tolerate outer space all that well.

[list]

"Governor Daza was really hesitant that time, Mr. FitzDavid. The Howayek lady didn't help." said one SummitONE executive warily, breaking the celebratory atmosphere of the group. "Do you think the El Howayeks are on your tail now?"

"When have they not been?" Gale said, chuckling as he patted his concerned colleague on the back. "The El Howayeks were always going to be suspicious, no matter what, though yes I was slightly surprised that even the Governor was joining in on the fad."

"Do you think we'll be able to proceed as is?" asked another.

"We'll be proceeding even if they put a thousand plants to watch our factories. Whatever prejudices they have against us, the fact of the matter is that Ardagan is dying. It has been for a long time now. In a dying world, people will be spending a helluva lot more resources into surviving, and that is where the mobile suits will come in handy. The Rosenmarqets thought they did something on Erene, but I'll show 
'em what it actually means to be a victor."

[/list]

Gale and company stepped into the maglev and vanished, speeding en route to their headquarters on the opposite end of the cylinder. Euphrasia peered out from beyond the huge onyx sign that she was hiding behind to eavesdrop on their conversation, her heart beat at last rising a little bit above the usual. "I guess that's it." she muttered, straightening out her hat and cleaning up her tunic. Gale wanted another war to show for and was actively looking for one. The issue now was where they'll go to find it.

The maglevs in the Orange Creek moved at an astonishing speed. Back on Erene, a maglev used to just speed along at around 600 km/h. Federation designs here though could reached nearly a thousand, specifically 965 km/h. By the time you missed a maglev, it'll be long gone, not that there was any tragedy to it, since another one will be right with you soon enough.

Still though, Gale hummed impatiently in his maglev seat. The world beyond the window distorted into a linear blur from the sheer speed of the rail, and still he felt he was wasting time. It wasn't just him either. Most corpos had some habit or another to express their annoyance with idling around. A tapping of the foot, a shaking leg, a finger tapping lightly onto a table. Gale himself made a habit of instinctively look at his watch over and over.

It was 1:07 PM, Vespurian Standard Time, exactly five minutes after he had step foot out of 11 League Park. During that time, he had traveled nearly 80 kilometers from 11 League Park. Back on Erene, you'd spend no less than three hours on the fastest roads just to get that far, and even still he felt as though the seconds were ticking by like tiny little fragments of opportunity costs. Two more minutes pass. 112 kilometers. Slowly, the maglev decelerated at a platform, and Gale would be the first one out, followed by the rest of his team.

[list]

"Tuesdays are horrible." Gale loudly proclaimed as he marched down the stairs and onto the streets en route to SummitONE Tower. "I swear, it's like every single stop they have to drop an entire field army off for some reason. Do we even have that many people?"

"Eight million's still a lot, FitzDavid."

"Sure, but on the premier maglev? Crap, it's like I was back to my regular days."

[/list]

Entering the sprawling skyscraper that figured prominently in the center of Sector 17, Gale wasted no time rushing into the elevator, away from the meandering regulars and middle management executives that constantly tried to suck up to him. Or rather, that's what he'd like to think. In general, the employees of a megacorporation will be antsy and servile if the owner were to suddenly come strolling around the workplace after all.

But Gale wasn't interested in mingling with the wage slaves, rather, he opted for tenth floor, where corporate's offices were located. A few of his colleagues would disperse here and there until only he remained, being as he was the only one among them authorized to be at corporate itself. Stepping off, Gale straightened his tunic and headed straight for his corner suit at the far end of the floor. There, a strange woman in what seemed to be a full suit of black combat armor stood idly by the front door. It was an New Security Instrument, or NSI. A kind of propriety clone soldier SummitONE occasionally produces for the Orange Guard.

[list]

"Any visits?" Gale briefly asked, heading straight for the door of his office.

"No." the NSI said bluntly, ending the conversation there and then.

"Great! Now, come inside, you look like a weird mannequin just standing around there. We learned a lot of lessons from the war with the Rosenmarqet." says Gale, opening the door entering his office, sitting down by his desk chair and relaxing before interfacing with his personal computer. "How's Frame 167 doing? No incidents so far?"

"Frame 167 has performed exactly to your standards, Mr. FitzDavid." the NSI replied, closing and locking the door behind her. "No faults were found in its armaments, while propulsion remained within your defined parameters. As you predicted, there were some issues during the unlock system when the 167s were deployed from the Wayfarers, but these have since been sorted out."

"Good. How'd it feel compared to a 164? Pretty good, huh?" asked Gale, finally smiling as he checked video footage of the experiments.

"Certainly the immense delta-v's of the 167 made maneuvering it much more complex given its intended purpose, but it was nothing this unit wasn't able to do."

"Say I were to stuff you into a 167 and told you to cause as much damage as you feasibly could in the shortest amount of time, would you do it?"

"If it is Mr. FitzDavid's will."

"Even if it means getting dropped in tin can on the far side of the world, alone, without any hope of return, with explicit orders to kill every man, woman, and child? Even if it means you'll have absolutely no hope of survival?"

"... I will do whatever is required of me." says the NSI, unfazed by Gale's questions.

"Good! That's good then. It's your lucky day then, because..."

[/list]

Gale dramatically turned in his office seat to the television screen embedded into the office wall, his arms theatrically pointing towards it. The NSI, confused, would turn to look at the screen. It had been turned off this entire time, but mysteriously turned on to the daily news. This was usually never done except in cases of immense geopolitical emergencies. 

The anchor's face looked grim, almost disheveled even, as she stared down at the file folder below.

[list]

"-... we don't know what's going on, but according to our partners over in Aktus the Local Korrin Authority had just declared independence from the Erene Federation under Chancellor Zytan Hoffmann. As you might recall from a previous news story, the LKA lost contact with the Federation over a technical glitch caused by an upsurge in Kartovsky particle activity. Federation officials now believe however that this had all been a ruse to-..."

[/list]

Suddenly, the screen went to black, Gale having turned off the broadcast. He turned to NSI, who nodded briefly, understanding the situation.

[list]

"Not bad huh? Go on then, get your mask and get out of here NSI. The Orange Guard will be waiting for you on a ship called the [i]Kispaga[/i]. Don't be late. Gen. Montagu will be there to tell you what you have to do."

"As you wish, Mr. FitzDavid." replies the NSI, turning around to exit the office. "It has been my greatest honor to have served you."

[/list][/spoiler]

[b][u]Presidential Speech[/u][/b]

It was customary for Presidents since the time of Ayub Khan, the founder of the Republic, to do yearly speeches at the opening of each Majlis session. Although Presidents occasionally made do without them, it was considered a useful way for Citizens to gauge the government's priorities for the year. President Fereydun Khan was unusual in that he neither gave a speech at the opening session of his new tricameral legislature nor at the subsequent session. The third session would be different and he indicated that he would revive the tradition.

At the expanded Majlis building, President Khan chose the House of Representatives chamber for the speech given that it was the largest of the three chambers, able to accomodate 500 people at once. The chamber was packed with Ministers, Representatives, Councillors, and Senators for the speech and included a select number of journalists and religious clergy as well.

Fereydun Khan walks up to the Speaker's podium and begins speaking:

[I]"In the name of Allah, the beneficent, the merciful.

Over the past few years Dhornaper has gone under a great transformation but so too has the world.

We have seen governments rise and fall, wars have been waged across the globe, terror and extremism has surged around us, but through it all, Dhornaper has remained stable and secure in its position. We have safeguarded our borders from war and resisted the tide of political extremism emanating from foreign powers. However, there are states that are engaging in expansionist colonial agendas on Shamatine soil. These states will not rest until Dhornaper is conquered or is a puppet. The government will continue to ensure the security of the state and will continue to develop our armed forces to counter hostile states and state sponsored extremism wherever it threatens Dhornaper. Colonial regimes will not be tolerated on our continent and we will commit ourselves to the liberation of West Shamat with our allies in the SSP.

Our economic situation has greatly improved in the past few years thanks to extensive reforms that enable unused resources to be utilised optimally. Importantly, the planning system has been simplified and construction works are progressing at an extraordinary pace. Housing prices across the cities have been declining and more Citizens are coming too the cities for work instead of being pushed out by high rents and property prices.

This has helped our industry enormously by shifting our population from less productive sectors towards more productive manufacturing and technology industries. These demographic changes, combined with the progress towards clean and reliable nuclear energy will make our manufacturing base stronger and more competitive by driving down energy costs.

My commitment to ensuring our security by resisting hostile states that enroach on Shamat soil and that promote political extremism will remain absolute as will my commitment towards investing in Dhornaper's infrastructure to expand our economy to help our Citizens.

God willing, Dhornaper's future will be safe from poverty and the tyranny of colonialism."[/i]

The Ministers and Majlis members give a round of applause while the clergy, dour as ever, appear to be pleased by the religious messaging in the speech, a rarity in Dhornaper's secular government. President Fereydun Khan walks off the Speaker's podium and makes his way to leave while the Majlis members begin to take their oaths and elect their Speakers.

[b]END OF THE WORLD[/b]

Zeon.

A name that up to date has been repeatedly misspelled as Zion, Zaeon, Zian, Zen, and the woefully named half region of Zeonia. It is a cold, arid, empty wasteland of a planet filled to the brim with resources, although barely a third the size of Erene all in all. Days can go on for many Erene months. It's cold. It's dark. It's dry. Only the most demented and inhuman of the lot would dare go that far to seek life.

This is where the Homunculi live.

These are not your common short lived ugly homunculi. These are perfect homunculi. Human shaped. Androgynous. Of all uses, chiefly labour and security. They don't eat, for they run on a philosopher's stone, and unless they live a life of excessive labour to fire it out, they'll go out and just cease working at a hundred or ninety years old, then be immediately cut up and harvested so their remains may make a homunculi replacement.

Homunculi are expensive to make. It takes a full Philosopher's Stone of abnormal size, between one to give sentient beings, alive or dead, plenty of bioengineering material and devices, a full year of crafting and rituals, chorographical organisation, and it overall costs a lot to craft from scratch, albeit for a worthwhile result. All homunculi are made, or born, in adult form, a blank slate, same face, same white hair, white eyes, pale skin, androgynous proportions. And then immediately given a task and sent to work.

Homunculi are endlessly resourceful. They have three great chief needs, or wants really. To construct, to create, as Homunculi are constructs inbedded with the endless desire of creation and engineering and crafting. Their other desire in "life" would be knowledge. They want to know. Know what? Anything really. But usually they restrict themselves to something useful. They are born knowing, and take to knowing easily. Any spare time is often spent in research or whatever it is they're crafting, or reading, or writing even. And their final will in this life mimicry, is to understand why they exist.

[b]THE ALCHEMIST[/b]

There was once a young boy, in the Old Montfleur, who moved to the big city from his Baronial Manor home, he met many people, he met nobles and priests, he met rabbi's and scholars, he met gypsies and knights, and he even met once an alchemist.

Evidently he reoccurred one more than the rest.

The boy grew up to understand alchemy, eventually becoming a Master of Alchemy on his own. To keep pretences since magic was frowned upon in Old Christian Elseyr, he wed, became a high standing clerk, had children, had a life. Which he immediately ended up on creating his most worthwhile creation. He fled, he left, he became a spentdrift of gold, he faked his death a dozen times and another dozen more, he travelled all of Erene to expand his knowledge.

He built a small shadow empire, for seven hundred years everything was fine. He had done rituals unimaginable. He had it all. Then, a century and a half ago, he almost had nothing again. Thankfully those seven centuries hadn't been spent just sitting about waiting for catastrophe to reach him. He prepared and thusly he survived again. At first, drifting, haunting the planet as it died, harvesting everything, all that he could, in the first decade of chaos.

Then, he went away, underground, hidden, interacting through proxy. He schemed, he scryed, he witnessed, and he planned. He sent funds where it benefited him, he talked and dealt with whom he could trust to do so, and spent his time perfecting the homunculus formula. And when the time came, he asked the Erene Federation, and got granted the rights to settle Zeon with his homunculi.

And he didn't waste a second, being the first to get there.

[b]LIFE ESSENCE[/b]

The method of making a philosopher's stone, is a secret.

It requires plenty of sacrifice, resources, method, and above all skill. From it, one can enact a Midas-like transfiguration of base metals into gold, although that had lost its use back when people began scanning every gold ounce for its mine of origin.

The primary use of the Philosopher's Stone is to brew the Elixir of Life. A rejuvenating healing panacean ichor concoction of similarly bright reddish hue. Physically fixing everything and de-aging the consumer by a few years with every gulp. Naturally this is assumed to be the height of alchemy for any alchemist. It is however, not.

Immortality is but a starting step in an alchemist's life, for there are two methods of progress in alchemy. Progress through Legacy and Progress through Life. One to merely accept failure and leave your work undone for others to complete, and the other to succeed and continue your research for however long you will it to.

[b]AZOTH[/b]

Azoth. Alchemical term for Mercury. Mercury. Elseryan Old God of Messengers and Health. Also an element on the periodic table. And something someone must drink before considering visiting the [i]Ardagan-Zeon-Ostanes Tactical Homebase[/i].

The Homunculi Colony. The Alchemist's Colony. One-Man Colony. The Azoth Autarchy. The Zeon Laboratory. The End-of-the-World Bastion. Mad Scientist's Basement. Monster Factory. House of Horrors. The Federation's Edge. Homunculi Hive. Or more normally, just Azoth.

It spanned an entire half of Zeon, covering it entirely in an automated and automaton ran industrial and resource extracting complex, the entire half of the planet coveted by the Homunculi. Underground, the colonies goes deeper. Into bases, laboratories, testing grounds, mines, artificial chambers, storage, and so on. Out in orbit, the colony runs communication satellites.

The surface of the industrial scientific military complex is armed with artillery, communication towers, defense stations. It's a bastion. A well armed and secure homebase. All to house the oldest alchemist in the world. Who is doing the old and honoured tradition of buying corpses for his experiments. He still tends to go scrying the other colonies and even Erene itself, but otherwise uncaring and uninvolved.

The colony is ran as an autocracy with the Alchemist as it's Autarch. Homunculi are given three names; their first name they choose themselves, from a list of available and permitted ones, their second name is a number, that of their craft order, counting even those dead, gone, or poorly crafted and scrapped. And lastly, their place of origin within the colony. Locations are, however, named a letter and a number and that's it, but for sake of simplicity they have codenames, often related to alchemy terms or old alchemists.

The homunculi treat the alchemist as their answer to the question as to why they exist; for him. Because that's what he tells them. They exist because of him, they exist because he made them, they should only exist for him, that's their entire purpose. The homunculi thus treat him as both father and god in a way, although he doesn't care that much, detached as he is of the affairs of his creations.

There is two million and five hundred thousand homunculi. And one human. The colony is ruled by the Alchemist, but governed by the most senior homunculi, who are led by the seniormost homunculi who are given the honorary title of 'Zero', in honour of the first and oldest true homunculi. Officially they're just labelled the Head of State and the rest as Ministers of Cabinet. Everyone is a denizen. Everyone has a job. Everyone has a meaning.

Everything is harmonious.

Everything is fine.

Until the new year began.

Independence. Independence everywhere.

And most unfortunately, right on their neighbour, too.

All homunculi are made, or born, in adult form, a blank slate, same face, same white hair, white eyes, pale skin, androgynous proportions. And then immediately given a task and sent to work.

Homunculi are endlessly resourceful. They have three great chief needs, or wants really. To construct, to create, as Homunculi are constructs inbedded with the endless desire of creation and engineering and crafting. Their other desire in "life" would be knowledge. They want to know. Know what? Anything really. But usually they restrict themselves to something useful. They are born knowing, and take to knowing easily. Any spare time is often spent in research or whatever it is they're crafting, or reading, or writing even. And their final will in this life mimicry, is to understand why they exist.

[b]THE ALCHEMIST[/b]

There was once a young boy, in the Old Montfleur, who moved to the big city from his Baronial Manor home, he met many people, he met nobles and priests, he met rabbi's and scholars, he met gypsies and knights, and he even met once an alchemist.

Evidently he reoccurred one more than the rest.

The boy grew up to understand alchemy, eventually becoming a Master of Alchemy on his own. To keep pretences since magic was frowned upon in Old Christian Elseyr, he wed, became a high standing clerk, had children, had a life. Which he immediately ended up on creating his most worthwhile creation. He fled, he left, he became a spentdrift of gold, he faked his death a dozen times and another dozen more, he travelled all of Erene to expand his knowledge.

He built a small shadow empire, for seven hundred years everything was fine. He had done rituals unimaginable. He had it all. Then, a century and a half ago, he almost had nothing again. Thankfully those seven centuries hadn't been spent just sitting about waiting for catastrophe to reach him. He prepared and thusly he survived again. At first, drifting, haunting the planet as it died, harvesting everything, all that he could, in the first decade of chaos.

Then, he went away, underground, hidden, interacting through proxy. He schemed, he scryed, he witnessed, and he planned. He sent funds where it benefited him, he talked and dealt with whom he could trust to do so, and spent his time perfecting the homunculus formula. And when the time came, he asked the Erene Federation, and got granted the rights to settle Zeon with his homunculi.

And he didn't waste a second, being the first to get there.

[b]LIFE ESSENCE[/b]

The method of making a philosopher's stone, is a secret.

It requires plenty of sacrifice, resources, method, and above all skill. From it, one can enact a Midas-like transfiguration of base metals into gold, although that had lost its use back when people began scanning every gold ounce for its mine of origin.

The primary use of the Philosopher's Stone is to brew the Elixir of Life. A rejuvenating healing panacean ichor concoction of similarly bright reddish hue. Physically fixing everything and de-aging the consumer by a few years with every gulp. Naturally this is assumed to be the height of alchemy for any alchemist. It is however, not.

Immortality is but a starting step in an alchemist's life, for there are two methods of progress in alchemy. Progress through Legacy and Progress through Life. One to merely accept failure and leave your work undone for others to complete, and the other to succeed and continue your research for however long you will it to.

[b]AZOTH[/b]

Azoth. Alchemical term for Mercury. Mercury. Elseryan Old God of Messengers and Health. Also an element on the periodic table. And something someone must drink before considering visiting the [i]Ardagan-Zeon-Ostanes Tactical Homebase[/i].

The Homunculi Colony. The Alchemist's Colony. One-Man Colony. The Azoth Autarchy. The Zeon Laboratory. The End-of-the-World Bastion. Mad Scientist's Basement. Monster Factory. House of Horrors. The Federation's Edge. Homunculi Hive. Or more normally, just Azoth.

It spanned an entire half of Zeon, covering it entirely in an automated and automaton ran industrial and resource extracting complex, the entire half of the planet coveted by the Homunculi. Underground, the colonies goes deeper. Into bases, laboratories, testing grounds, mines, artificial chambers, storage, and so on. Out in orbit, the colony runs communication satellites.

The surface of the industrial scientific military complex is armed with artillery, communication towers, defense stations. It's a bastion. A well armed and secure homebase. All to house the oldest alchemist in the world. Who is doing the old and honoured tradition of buying corpses for his experiments. He still tends to go scrying the other colonies and even Erene itself, but otherwise uncaring and uninvolved.

The colony is ran as an autocracy with the Alchemist as it's Autarch. Homunculi are given three names; their first name they choose themselves, from a list of available and permitted ones, their second name is a number, that of their craft order, counting even those dead, gone, or poorly crafted and scrapped. And lastly, their place of origin within the colony. Locations are, however, named a letter and a number and that's it, but for sake of simplicity they have codenames, often related to alchemy terms or old alchemists.

The homunculi treat the alchemist as their answer to the question as to why they exist; for him. Because that's what he tells them. They exist because of him, they exist because he made them, they should only exist for him, that's their entire purpose. The homunculi thus treat him as both father and god in a way, although he doesn't care that much, detached as he is of the affairs of his creations.

There is two million and five hundred thousand homunculi. And one human. The colony is ruled by the Alchemist, but governed by the most senior homunculi, who are led by the seniormost homunculi who are given the honorary title of 'Zero', in honour of the first and oldest true homunculi. Officially they're just labelled the Head of State and the rest as Ministers of Cabinet. Everyone is a denizen. Everyone has a job. Everyone has a meaning.

Everything is harmonious.

Everything is fine.

Until the new year began.

Independence. Independence everywhere.

And most unfortunately, right on their neighbour, too.
[/spoiler]
